name: Bavette's Bar & Boeuf
review:
From the warm lighting, cozy ambiance to the the amount of care in presentation, taste, and balance in each dish here, this restaurant continues to be one of my favorite in all of Chicago.

While you won’t go wrong with any dish on the menu, some of my favorites include the baked goat cheese, the smoked salmon caesar salad, and the fried (boneless) chicken.

One thing that doesn’t nearly get enough attention on the menu is the burger. It’s truly exquisite. I recommend splitting it into halves or quarters to share, because it’s so rich but so delicious.

name: Armitage Alehouse
review:
We loved everything about this restaurant, but before I talk about the food, I have to praise the old-school ambiance, the friendly, passionate waiters, and excellent service from start to finish. We ordered around 8-9 dishes and the waiters divided our order into “courses” and guided us through a multi-course dining experience to ensure we savor each dish before the next comes out. We got new plates and silverware 5 times throughout our meal, and got our water refilled at least 15 times throughout our meal.

Onto the food, every dish is cooked and presented well, it’s hard to go wrong with anything, it really comes down to personal preference and whatever flavors you like the most.

Pot pies (today was chicken + steak). Our group raved about these, the pastry was cooked to perfection, all of the veggies and flavors inside came together extremely well. This was my personal favorite dish out of everything we got.

The prime rib sandwich was also a flavor bomb - the bread was thin and light, but absorbed the au jus so well. The meat was fatty and thin, reminding me of a cheesesteak but with elevated ingredients.

The tikka masala was good - large chunks of chicken and it was fairly authentic, a little spicy and less creamy, though catered to a modern American palette (along with the naan). Not sure if it was served with the 2 year aged Basmati rice with it.

I wish they served garlic naan instead of the naans they had, they felt more Mediterranean than Indian to me.

The chutney and whipped feta were good, both were yogurt-based creamy dips that we kept gravitating towards throughout each dish.

The Wagyu double cheeseburger felt a little out of place with the other dishes but was awesome! I loved the fries, they were fried in beef tallow, I think, and the aioli paired so well with it. The smash burger felt steep for 30 dollars but it was cooked to perfection, with lacy bits of beef around the edges. Our group finished our portions of the burger so fast.

The tandoori chicken is a bit of a misname, it should be called barbeque chicken. But that’s not a knock on the dish - it was, once again, cooked until extremely tender and it had a good glaze on it (shoutout to the veggies it came with).

Last but not least, the sticky date cake (and free gelato we got for a birthday in our group) were both excellent desserts. The sticky date cake reminded me of Gordon Ramsay’s sticky toffee pudding dessert, but this was honestly better - more pronounced toffee, shortbread cookie, and brown butter gelato all added to the flavors.

If it weren’t this hard to get a reservation at a reasonable time, I’d come back to this place all the time. But I get why this place has the hype, it deserves it.

name: Gretel
review:
Hands down my favorite burger in the city. It’s the most upscale fast food style burger and I mean that in the best way possible.

The mac and cheese was so good too. My only (super small) critique is that the noodle shape is not my favorite for Mac and cheese. But the flavors and cheesiness were on point.

The elote was tasty but would prefer it without the “rib” of the corn.

The nachos sounded good but I expected pulled pork and didn’t feel like there was enough when it was actually served.

name: Mott St
review:
Excellent, excellent burger - truly among the best you can get in the city.

It’s juicy, rich thanks to the miso butter. The onions aren’t as crispy as you’d think but that’s okay, it’s still absolutely delicious.

I want to come back and try everything on the menu.

name: Bistro Campagne
review:
I loved the intimate ambiance, great portions, and excellent drinks. Every time I go to a French restaurant, I walk away with a really good meal and an elite dining experience. Bistro Campagne was no different.

The fortified wine was served like a glass of whiskey but tasted so much lighter.

The escargot was very tender and served with oil and herbs and a baguette.

We each got a French onion soup and it was hearty but nothing super special. The onions could’ve been cooked down even more.

The steak tartare was creamy, served with mushrooms, and crusty chips, but not very traditional. I would’ve loved to just have the meat to let the flavors and beefiness shine without all of the additional flavors. Some who don’t want the raw meat taste may prefer this, though.

The mac and cheese and the special potato side dish we got was a little underwhelming. Still tasty, but we’ve had better renditions of each elsewhere. I didn’t need the herbs to be all over the mac and cheese, and I thought it could’ve been creamier. I was hoping the potatoes would be something more bite sized instead of looking like a slice of pie (or cheesecake).

The steak in the steak frites were cooked perfectly and the fries were a little soggy but the perfect texture and consistency. Next time I go back, I’d love to try the duck leg or the black cod. Too bad very few reviews mention either dish.

The bread pudding was my favorite of the three desserts, but I enjoyed the basque cheesecake.

Overall, this is an awesome date spot and the food and experience is really high quality.

name: Ever Restaurant
review:
This is quite a special experience. You’re treated like royalty from the moment you walk in and it feels like you’re eating in a cave.

The 7 course + 2 dessert meal was special from start to finish, and the wines that accompanied continued to elevate the experience.

This is pure luxury and has ambiance better than most 3 Michelin star restaurants.

Although the food was simply incredible, I think the elite service, cleanliness and attention to detail, the amazing furniture, seeing the ingredients hung on the ceiling before walking to your table, and the ability to tour the kitchen after the meal all just made for an extremely memorable night.
